checks_performed: Read the exact unrestricted target and the draft; no other source material or web resources were used.

Independently derived the centered-projector decomposition, completion criterion, reconstruction and tensor identities, fourth-moment consequence, purity budget, real-ray bound, and tensor-product reductions.
Ran an exact Eisenstein-integer enumeration for the dimension-three common-unbiased rays and orthogonal triples.

Investigated the omitted mixed fourth/sixth-root case. A mixed vector pair invalidates the draft's pairwise shortcut, but a complete exact basis enumeration independently proves the stated basis bound.
Enumerated dephased BH(6,4) and BH(6,6) bases and all necessary relative twelfth-root phases using integer cyclotomic arithmetic; all 1,123,200 cases were rejected without floating point.
Enumerated all order-six subgroups of Z_6^2, checked isotropy and pairwise intersections, and confirmed the maximum compatible family has size three.

claims.claim: For pairwise MUBs, their centered rank-one projectors span mutually orthogonal five-dimensional traceless diagonal subspaces; seven MUBs are equivalent to an orthogonal decomposition of the 35-dimensional traceless Hermitian space into seven such subspaces.
claims.evidence: For Q_ki=P_ki-I/6, Tr(Q_kiQ_kj)=δ_ij-1/6, whose Gram matrix has rank five, while cross-basis products are zero exactly under mutual unbiasedness. Seven orthogonal five-dimensional spaces fill the 35-dimensional traceless Hermitian space, and the converse follows from Tr(P_kiP_lj)=1/6.
claims.search_method: Direct Hilbert–Schmidt calculation and dimension count.

claims.claim: Given any six MUBs in C^6, let W be the orthogonal complement of their six centered diagonal subspaces. They extend to a seventh MUB if and only if every pair of matrices in W commutes; if so, the extension is unique.
claims.evidence: The six subspaces occupy dimension 30, so W has dimension five. An extension has centered diagonal space W. Conversely, commuting Hermitian elements of W are simultaneously diagonalizable; dimension equality makes W the full traceless diagonal space in that eigenbasis. Orthogonality gives unbiasedness, and the full diagonal algebra has one-dimensional joint eigenspaces, proving uniqueness up to phases and permutation.
claims.search_method: Dimension count, simultaneous diagonalization, and diagonal-algebra uniqueness.

claims.claim: A complete set of seven MUBs satisfies the reconstruction identity Σ_ki Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I and the tensor identity Σ_ki P_ki⊗P_ki=I+F.
claims.evidence: Each centered simplex is Parseval on its five-dimensional subspace, and the seven subspaces orthogonally decompose the traceless space. Restoring the scalar component yields the reconstruction formula. Pairing it with an arbitrary B gives Tr(AB)+Tr(A)Tr(B), exactly the trace pairing of A⊗B with F+I; product matrices span the tensor matrix space.
claims.search_method: Simplex frame-operator calculation and nondegenerate tensor trace pairing.

claims.claim: In a complete set, every unit vector x obeys Σ_ki |⟨x,v_ki⟩|^4=2; a vector unbiased to any chosen six bases must be a ray of the remaining basis.
claims.evidence: Pairing the reconstruction identity for P_x with P_x gives the sum 2. Six unbiased bases contribute exactly 1. The remaining probabilities satisfy Σp_i=Σp_i²=1; nonnegativity then forces one probability to equal one and all others zero.
claims.search_method: Application of the reconstruction identity followed by an exact probability argument.

claims.claim: For any hypothetical complete set and any fixed identification C^6=C^2⊗C^3, the sum of the 42 qubit reduced purities is exactly 30.
claims.evidence: The partial-swap formula converts each purity to Tr[P⊗P(F_A⊗I_BB)]. Substitution of I+F_A⊗F_B gives Tr(F_A)Tr(I_BB)+Tr(I_AA)Tr(F_B)=2·9+4·3=30.

claims.claim: Relative to any fixed C^2⊗C^3 factorization, a complete set contains at most 18 product rays and at most three entirely product bases. Equality forces every other ray to be maximally entangled.
claims.evidence: Every qubit reduced purity is at least 1/2, while a product ray contributes 1. Thus P product rays force total purity at least P+(42-P)/2=21+P/2; comparison with 30 gives P≤18. Equality forces every remaining purity to be 1/2, exactly maximal entanglement. Three product bases already attain P=18.
claims.search_method: Purity extremality and the exact total-purity budget.

claims.claim: For any fixed conjugation K, a complete set has at most 12 K-real rays and hence at most two bases consisting entirely of K-real rays.
claims.evidence: In K-real coordinates, Ω=Σ_re_r⊗e_r gives ⟨Ω,P_v⊗P_v Ω⟩=|Σ_rv_r²|²≤1, with equality exactly for a K-invariant ray. The tensor identity makes the sum of these nonnegative statistics ⟨Ω,(I+F)Ω⟩=12, so at most 12 rays, hence at most two six-ray bases, can be K-real.
claims.search_method: Tensor-moment evaluation against the maximally correlated vector Ω.

claims.claim: Two direct tensor-product bases in C^2⊗C^3 are mutually unbiased if and only if their respective qubit bases and qutrit bases are mutually unbiased.
claims.evidence: Squared product overlaps factor as α_rsβ_tu. If every product is 1/6, fixing t,u makes all α_rs equal; row normalization forces α_rs=1/2 and then β_tu=1/3. Conversely, multiplying local unbiased overlaps gives 1/6.
claims.search_method: Factorization of tensor-product overlaps and stochastic row sums.

claims.claim: Every triple of MUBs in C^3 extends uniquely to four MUBs, and the rays unbiased to all three are exactly the fourth basis.
claims.evidence: After reducing the first pair to the standard and Fourier bases, exact enumeration gives precisely six common-unbiased rays. Their orthogonality graph consists of exactly two triples, and every cross-triple overlap has squared magnitude 1/3. Choosing either triple as the third basis therefore leaves exactly the other as the unique fourth basis and common-unbiased locus.
claims.search_method: Standard/Fourier normalization followed by exact arithmetic in Z[ω].

claims.claim: If three unit qubit rays form a tight frame with frame operator 3I/2 and are all unbiased to one qubit basis, that basis is the unique qubit basis unbiased to all three rays.
claims.evidence: The three centered projectors lie in the two-dimensional off-diagonal plane and sum to zero. They cannot span a line because three equal-norm signed collinear vectors cannot sum to zero, so they span that plane. A basis unbiased to all three must have its diagonal traceless axis in the unique orthogonal line, which determines the original unordered basis.
claims.search_method: Centered-projector geometry in the three-dimensional real qubit Bloch space.

claims.claim: No maximally entangled vector in C^2⊗C^3 is unbiased to three pairwise MUB direct tensor-product bases.
claims.evidence: Uniform product probabilities make the orthogonal complement w of the qutrit Schmidt support unbiased to the three local qutrit bases, so claim 8 places w in their fourth basis. Expanding the state over the other two fourth-basis rays produces, for each local qutrit basis, three normalized conditional qubit rays forming a 3I/2 tight frame. They are unbiased both to a fixed Schmidt qubit basis and to the corresponding local qubit basis. Claim 9 forces all three local qubit bases to coincide, contradicting their pairwise mutual unbiasedness.
claims.search_method: Schmidt-support reduction, conditional-state tight frames, and claims 8–9.

claims.claim: A complete seven-MUB set in C^2⊗C^3 cannot contain three direct tensor-product bases; consequently it contains at most two such bases.
claims.evidence: Three direct tensor-product bases provide 18 product rays. Claim 5 then forces all remaining 24 rays to be maximally entangled, but each would be unbiased to the three product bases, contradicting claim 10.
claims.search_method: Combination of the exact purity budget with the maximally-entangled-vector obstruction.

claims.claim: If one basis is standard and every vector in every other basis has coordinates consisting entirely of fourth roots, or entirely of sixth roots, divided by √6, then the MUB family has at most two bases.
claims.evidence: The draft's same-alphabet modular arguments are correct, but its immediate exclusion of mixed vector pairs is false: such pairs exist. The conclusion nevertheless survives. Same-alphabet impossibility forces any two nonstandard MUBs to be one pure BH(6,4) and one pure BH(6,6). The exact checker enumerates 72 dephased BH(6,4) bases, confirms they form one relevant monomial orbit, enumerates 312 dephased BH(6,6) bases and 3,600 necessary relative twelfth-root phase choices, and rejects all 1,123,200 cases.
claims.search_method: Complete integer-cyclotomic enumeration in Z[ζ_12], including alphabet reduction, Butson bases, monomial orbit coverage, and relative row phases.

claims.claim: For the standard dimension-six Weyl construction, order-six isotropic subgroups L≤Z_6^2 give stabilizer bases, and two such bases are mutually unbiased exactly when their label subgroups intersect only at zero.
claims.evidence: Isotropy makes the six labelled Weyl operators a commuting, star-closed, six-dimensional algebra in M_6. A commutative unital algebra of dimension six acting on C^6 has six rank-one joint eigenspaces, giving a stabilizer basis. Weyl trace orthogonality makes two traceless diagonal algebras orthogonal exactly when their nonzero label sets are disjoint, equivalently L∩M={0}; claim 0 then gives mutual unbiasedness.
claims.search_method: Weyl commutator and trace-orthogonality proof, supported by exact subgroup enumeration.

claims.claim: At most three pairwise MUB stabilizer bases arise from the dimension-six Weyl construction, and three are attainable.
claims.evidence: Every order-six subgroup contains a nonzero involution, while Z_6^2 has only (3,0), (0,3), and (3,3). Pairwise trivial intersections require distinct involutions, giving at most three subgroups. The horizontal, vertical, and diagonal cyclic subgroups attain three. Exact enumeration found 12 order-six isotropic subgroups and maximum compatible-family size three.
claims.search_method: Involution counting plus exhaustive exact enumeration in Z_6^2.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a proof that no seven MUBs exist in C^6 or an exact construction of seven. The draft supplies neither and explicitly says the unrestricted arbitrary-phase, non-stabilizer case remains open. Its verified projector reductions, uniqueness result, moment identities, entanglement restrictions, and exact obstructions for direct-product, finite-phase, and Weyl-stabilizer subclasses are material but incomplete progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate rather than FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET or OVERCLAIMED. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, which accurately describes this coverage.
